title: How NASA Fixed Voyager 1 From 15 Billion Miles Away

subtitles.text: In late 2023, Voyager 1 went completely silent 15 billion miles away.
Built in 1977, Voyager runs on vintage triple-redundant flight computers.
JPL engineers performed code surgery across space to save the mission.

scenes.narration: In late 2023, Voyager 1 went completely silent, sending back nothing but raw repetitive binary noise across fifteen billion miles.
scenes.visualPrompt: Voyager 1 deep space probe drifting amidst stars in the cold void

scenes.narration: Built in 1977, Voyager runs on triple-redundant flight computers with mere kilobytes of memory routing vintage assembly code.
scenes.visualPrompt: Vintage 1970s spacecraft circuit board with ceramic microchips and glowing buses

scenes.narration: JPL engineers found a single fried memory chip and performed code surgery across space, bringing the probe back to life.
scenes.visualPrompt: NASA mission control room monitors lighting up green with telemetry data
